Quick Read

SNAP generated $706 million in trailing free cash flow across 8 straight positive quarters, even as the stock fell 32% in 2026.

RDDT fell 36% and PINS dropped 27% in 2026, confirming that SNAP's decline is a sector problem, not a company-specific collapse.

Snap's 9% ad revenue growth and unresolved youth-safety litigation keep the stock split between real cash value and meaningful legal risk.

A broad selloff in social media stocks sits behind the slide in Snap (NYSE:SNAP) stock, and that shared decline is the first thing the bargain-or-toxic question has to account for. Snap stock is down 32% this year to $5.47. Shares are up 1% in afternoon trading.

Wikimedia Commons (Maurizio Pesce)

For comparison, Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) stock is down 36% this year to $147.75, a steeper slide than the one in Snap stock. Meanwhile, Pinterest (NYSE:PINS) stock is down 27% this year to $18.98, a softer decline pointing in the same direction. The three ad-funded platforms have moved lower together.

To gauge how far social media has fallen behind, the Global X Social Media ETF (NASDAQ:SOCL) is down 21% this year. However, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 12% this year. That gap places Snap's decline inside a sector problem first, with company-specific questions layered on top.

Cash Flow Anchors the Bargain Case

Snap's quarterly earnings call in early August supplied most of the evidence for the bargain argument. Chief executive and co-founder Evan Spiegel stated that Snapchat is "approaching 1 billion people using our service every month." Spiegel further declared that free cash flow per share will be Snap's primary financial objective going forward.

A 39-year-old retired with $700,000 even though a lot of people didn't think it was enough. A decade later, their portfolio is now worth as much as $1.5 million, despite spending those years living off their investments.

"Honestly the market wasn't what got tested, I was," they shared on Reddit.

They Never Earned Six Figures, But Saved 70% For 11 Years

The poster didn't build their portfolio on a huge salary. The most they ever made in a year was $75,000, but they were single with no children and saved 70% of their income for 11 years. That included money they put toward paying off their house.

Snap Inc. (NYSE:SNAP) stock is jumping 6% to $5.66 Wednesday as investors weigh improving operating momentum against significant legal and regulatory pressure. The move puts Snap well ahead of the broader market, with social-media peers also showing mixed action.

stockcam / Getty Images

Snap's latest results have given investors reasons to focus on improving fundamentals, including 19% revenue growth in the second quarter and stronger cash generation. At the same time, regulatory scrutiny surrounding teen safety and potential product restrictions remains an important risk for Snap's engagement, costs and longer-term growth.

Snap's Fundamentals Improve

Snap's second-quarter performance showed momentum across several parts of the business, with revenue increasing 19% from a year earlier. The company is also expanding beyond its traditional advertising business through artificial-intelligence glasses and a broader push into business-to-business advertising.

The focus on AI glasses gives Snap another potential growth avenue as the company looks to build products beyond its core social-media platform. Snap's B2B advertising efforts could also help diversify revenue, although the company continues to operate in a competitive digital advertising market.

Legal and regulatory pressure remains the biggest counterweight to the improving operating picture. The company faces scrutiny involving teen safety, while potential product restrictions could affect user engagement and increase compliance-related costs.

Reddit Stock Rises on Its Own

Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) stock is also moving higher, gaining 4% to $151.24. The move gives Reddit a stronger session than the broader market and puts another major social-media platform in positive territory alongside Snap.

title: Reddit Is Growing Above 40% a Year, So Why Is the Stock Down 40%?
detail:
Reddit Is Growing Above 40% a Year, So Why Is the Stock Down 40%?
David Beren
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:28 AM CDT 4 min read
RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Reddit Is Growing Above 40% a Year, So Why Is the Stock Down 40%? ©Brett Jordan from Pexels, Karola G from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Reddit closed at $145.35 on September 29, down about 40% this year and roughly 45% below its 52-week high of $263.50.

Second-quarter revenue grew 61% to $805 million at a 43% adjusted EBITDA margin, and consensus expects around 54% revenue growth this year.

TIKR's model shows the P/E multiple down around 38% over the past year while earnings grew, so the drop in the shares comes from a lower multiple.

Third-quarter revenue guidance of $860 million to $870 million sets up the next test of how quickly growth is slowing.

Revenue Growth Is Still Strong but Slowing

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) runs a user-generated content platform that earns money mainly from advertising, plus premium subscriptions and data licensing. Revenue reached $2.2 billion in fiscal 2025, up 69% from $1.3 billion.

In the second quarter, it grew 61% to $805 million, and daily active unique users rose 18% to 130.3 million. The chart below adds consensus estimates through fiscal 2030.

Reddit Revenue Estimates. (TIKR)

Analysts expect revenue near $3.4 billion this year, up around 54%, then around $4.5 billion in fiscal 2027 and around $7.7 billion by fiscal 2030, roughly 3.5 times the fiscal 2025 level.

Growth slows steadily along the way, from around 54% this year to around 32% in fiscal 2027 and around 17% by fiscal 2030. Reddit's own third-quarter guidance is $860 million to $870 million.

Pinterest, another advertising-funded platform built on user content, grew second-quarter revenue 18% at a 26% adjusted EBITDA margin, against 61% and 43% at Reddit.

Profits Are Scaling With the Business

Profits have kept pace with growth. Normalized EPS rose from $2.45 in fiscal 2024 to $4.54 in fiscal 2025, up around 85%, and second-quarter net income was $253 million, or 31% of revenue.

Free cash flow reached $261 million in the quarter, Reddit repurchased $235 million of its stock, and it holds about $2.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. The chart below shows consensus estimates through fiscal 2030.

Reddit EPS Normalized. (TIKR)

Analysts expect EPS of around $7.70 this year, around $9.70 in fiscal 2027, and around $13 by fiscal 2030. This year's earnings are expected to grow around 69% against around 54% for revenue, then slow to around 26% in fiscal 2027.

Estimates barely move between fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029, so the outer years deserve less weight than the near-term figures.

Should You Buy Reddit Stock?

TIKR's valuation model connects growth and margins to a possible return, starting from the September 29 price of $145.35.

Over the past year, it shows the shares down around 28% and the P/E multiple down around 38%. The decline came from a lower multiple, since earnings grew over the same stretch.

A 22-year-old teacher lost both parents in a car accident and received about $150,000 from their military life insurance policies. The check is still sitting in its envelope while they try to figure out what to do with money they never expected to have.

"I truly don't know what to do with this," they shared on Reddit.

They Had Already Made It Through College Without Debt

The poster grew up poor but worked their way through university and graduated without student loans. They had also paid off their car three months earlier and were living in a small one-bedroom apartment.

Their first-year teaching salary didn't leave much extra, but they were getting by without debt and wanted to keep living modestly. Rather than spend the $150,000, they hoped to put it somewhere it could grow while still having access to the money if they needed it.

What they didn't have was much experience managing money, especially an amount this large. Losing both parents only made it harder to think about what should happen next.

"Honestly, having the money just feels really shi**y and the grief makes it hard to think about clearly," the poster said.

The Check Didn't Have To Change Anything Yet

Most people advised the poster not to make any major decisions with the inheritance while the loss was still so recent.

"Grieve. Wait. Read and learn about options," someone wrote.

In the meantime, commenters suggested depositing the check and keeping the money in a high-yield savings account while the original poster considered their options. People also raised an emergency fund, a Roth IRA and longer-term investing as possibilities once they were ready to make those decisions.
